purpose.domain_detail: Appears to be a French-language banking or financial application (variable names like NCPTEI suggest account/counter numbers, CLRIB0 suggests a Luhn/modulo-97 check digit calculation typical of IBAN or Belgian/French bank account validation); program name SPGRYNRB and constants reference 'DPR' application code
purpose.summary: This CICS online program validates financial account identifiers using a modulo-97 check digit algorithm (similar to IBAN validation). It receives data via DFHCOMMAREA, validates account codes and counters, computes a check digit by dividing by 97, and returns results. It also performs date format conversion between multiple date representations.

notable_features: EXEC CICS PUSH HANDLE / POP HANDLE for condition handling
EXEC CICS HANDLE ABEND with label
EXEC CICS ASKTIME / FORMATTIME for current date/time retrieval
EXEC CICS RETURN for transaction return
Modulo-97 check digit calculation (DIVIDE 97 INTO ... REMAINDER)
Extensive date format conversion subroutine (F9520) supporting multiple date layouts
Heavy use of GO TO for paragraph flow control (25 GOTOs)
REDEFINES used for overlay of date and working storage areas
French-language variable and comment naming conventions
verdict.notes: Program constants embed a generation date of 28/02/2003 and program identifiers suggesting this is from a French or Belgian financial system (PAC framework, 'DPR' application). The modulo-97 algorithm and field names (NCPTEI, CLRIB0) strongly suggest Belgian/French bank account number validation. No COPY statements present; all logic is self-contained. Comment ratio is very low (1 comment line).
